candidate_relations.reason: Knee pain after streptokinase is a serum-sickness feature, not a primary reactive arthritis diagnosis.
Streptokinase-induced hemolytic anemia is unsupported: LDH is negative and there is no hemolysis work-up proving hemolysis.
Coagulation changes with INR 2.5 in an anticoagulated valve patient do not establish DIC as the syndrome.
Poststreptococcal reactive arthritis follows streptococcal infection, not pharmacologic streptokinase exposure.
There is no antiphospholipid serology or thrombotic APS phenotype supporting that diagnosis.
Hemoglobin 9.65 g/dL without documented hemolysis is not hemolytic anemia and is not serum sickness.
Streptokinase-induced hemolysis is an incompatible mechanism for this delayed fever-arthralgia syndrome.
Autoimmune disorder is a vague parent that does not identify serum sickness.
None does not identify the reference diagnosis of serum sickness.
Anemia is a laboratory finding, not serum sickness.
A therapeutic/high INR from anticoagulation is not a bleeding-disorder diagnosis and is not serum sickness.

case_quality_flags: No candidate names serum sickness despite fever and arthralgia two weeks after streptokinase.
Platelet count of 4,456,000/µL is physiologically implausible and likely a transcription error.
